question: Goods and Service Tax is an example of ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**indirect tax.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goods and Service Tax (GST)** is a type of** indirect tax** that is levied on the** sale of goods and services.**
 
• It is an example of an **indirect tax** because it is **not directly paid by the consumer** to the government, but rather collected by **businesses** and then** remitted** to the government.
 
• **GST** was introduced in India in **2017** to replace** multiple indirect taxes** such as **excise duty, service tax, and value-added tax (VAT).**
 
• The aim was to simplify the tax system and create a **single, unified tax structure.**
 
• The GST system has **different tax rates** for different goods and services, ranging from **0% to 28%.**
 
• There are four tax slabs **- 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28% -** with essential goods and services attracting lower rates and luxury items attracting higher rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Compensation to employees **is a payment made by an **employer to an employee** in return for their work. It is** not related** to GST.
 
• **Direct tax **is a tax that is paid directly by an** individual or organization** to the government, such as income tax or corporate tax. GST is **not** a direct tax.
 
• **Transfer payment **is a type of payment made by the **government to individuals or organizations **without any goods or services being exchanged.
 
 
• Examples include **social security** benefits and welfare payments. This is also** not r**elated to GST.
 
 
 
• Hence, the **correct **answer is option 4 - GST is an example of an indirect tax.
